sentences.text:
Author: Surepalli Nanda
Bench: Surepalli Nanda
 Hon'Ble Mrs Justice Surepalli Nanda
 Writ Petition No.22799 Of 2020
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue (Land Acquisition) and learned Additional Advocate General, appearing on behalf of the respondents.
2. The petitioner has approached this Court, seeking the following relief:
"to issue a writ/order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of mandamus to (a) Declare the notification under Sec 11(1) in proceedings No.G1/346/2018 dated 27.10.2018 in respect of petitioners lands admeasuring Ac.3-03 gts., situated in Sy.Nos.18/E, 48, 59, 60, 61, 176/AA, 177/A, 177/AA2 at Kamaram Village, Shankarampet (R) Mandal, Medak District as illegal, arbitrary,
unconstitutional and contrary to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013) and to consequently set aside the same (b) Declare the proceedings of the Respondent No 3 in proceedings no. G1/346/2018-9 dated 24-09-2020 as illegal, arbitrary, unconstitutional and violative of Sec 11, Sec. 15(2), Sec 19(7) and sec 26 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013) (c) To declare the rejection letter of the respondents nos. 3 and 4 dated 21.10.2020 in letter no.C/1786/2018 as illegal arbitrary and unconstitutional and contrary to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013) more specifically Sec.26 and 27 of the Act, 2013 and the Telangana Revision of Market Value Guidelines Rules, 1998 (d) in the alternative direct the Respondents to give land for land compensation in the same village i.e., Kamaram or any other surrounding village with same potentiality for an equal extent of Ac.3-03 gts."
3. This Court vide its order dated 16.12.2020 passed interim order in I.A.No.1 of 2020 in W.P.No.22799 of 2020, and in particular, the relevant para, reads as under:
"In that view of the matter, prima faice, the acquisition proceedings initiated under Section 11 would be liable to be set aside.

Inasmuch as Section 38 of the Land Acquisition Act mandates that unless the Award is made and the compensation R Mahesh Reddy vs State Of Telangana on 12 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191016818/
1 amount is paid, no possession can be taken, there shall be interim stay of all further proceedings including making of Award pursuant to the impugned Notification.
Learned Special Government Pleader A.Sanjay Kumar takes notice.

sentences.text: So far as the first ground is concerned, the matter is required to be considered in due course.

Respondents are at liberty to move a vacate petition."
4.

In pursuance to filing of the writ petition in the year 2020, the 4th respondent made an Endorsement vide proceedings Letter No.C/1786/2018 dated 14.06.2023 stating that there is a deviation in the proposed alignment for 290 metres length along the roadside i.e., right side to the actual alignment so as to make the Kamaram tank (Oora Cheruvu) as Balancing Reservoir and the District Collector, Medak had accorded permission for change in alignment that is starting from KM. 23.225 to KM. 24.000 of the Shankarampet Branch canal (Main canal) as the canal to be diverted from KM.23.225 with a length of 290 meters along the roadside i.e., right side to the actual alignment so as to make the Kamaram Tank (Oora Cheruvu) as Balancing Reservoir.

Further the petitioner was informed that the land of the petitioner and his family members in Sy.No.176 and 177 which was previously sought to be acquired has been dropped in light of the endorsement dated 14.06.2023.
It is also observed in the said letter dated 14.06.2023 that the deviation in the alignment is helpful for providing discharge and velocity as designed for the canal so as to reach the tail end.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner brings on record a Memo vide USR No.1 of 2023 dated 28.06.2023, which reads as under:
"The respondent No.4 vide endorsement bearing Lr.No.C/1786/2018 dated 14.06.2023 has deviated the alignment for 290 meters length along the roadside i.e.,
right side to the actual alignment so as to make the Kamaram tank (Oora Cheruvu) as Balancing Reservoir.

Due to the said deviation land admeasuring Ac.5-19 gts.,
situated at Sy.No.128/AA/1(Ac.1-00 gts.), 128/A/1/1 (Ac.1-12 gts.), 177/A/2 (Ac.0-27 gts.), 177/A (Ac.0-28 gts.), 176/A (Ac.0-25 gts.), 178/A2 (Ac.0-31 gts.), 178/AA (Ac.0-13 gts.) and 179/AA (Ac.0-03 gts.) at Kamaram Village, Shankarampet (R)
Mandal, Medak District which was previously requisitioned will not be acquired or compensated.

The petitioner was informed that the land of the petitioner and his family members in Sy.No.176 and 177 which was previously sought to be acquired has been dropped in light of the endorsement dated 14.06.2023.

The notification under Section 11(1) in proceedings No.G1/346/2018 dated 27.10.2018 is liable to be set aside in respect of Sy.No.176 and 177 in light of the endorsement bearing Lr.No.C1/1786/2018 dated 14.06.2023.
The petitioner is attaching a copy of the endorsement bearing Lr.No.C/1786/2018 dated 14-06-2023 for consideration by this Hon'ble Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has no objection for acquisition of the remaining extent of land in Sy.Nos.18/E, 48, 59, 60, 61 at Kamaram Village, Shankarampet (R) Mandal, Medak District if the respondents seek to acquire the same after paying compensation to the petitioner as per the prevailing market rates.

In these circumstances, the interim order dated 16.12.2020 may be vacated and the Hon'ble Court may consider the petitioner's submissions and dispose of the writ petition as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and necessary in the interest of justice.
Hence, this Memo."

6. Taking into consideration the contents of the Memo filed by the petitioner vide USR No.1 of 2023 dated 28.06.2023 (referred to and extracted above), and duly considering that the land of the petitioner and his family members in Sy.Nos.176 and 177, which was previously sought to be acquired has been dropped in the light of the endorsement vide letter No.C/1786/2018 dated 14.06.2023, and also taking into consideration the fact that the petitioner has no objection for acquisition of the remaining extent of land in survey Nos.18/E, 48, 59, 60, 61 at Kamaram Village,
Shankarampet (R) Mandal, Medak District if the same is acquired by the respondent authorities by paying compensation to the petitioner as per the rules and as per prevailing market rates, the writ petition is disposed of directing the respondents, to consider the acquisition of the remaining extent of petitioner's land in Survey Nos. 18/E, 48, 59, 60, 61 at Kamaram Village, Shankarampet (R)
Mandal, Medak District, by following due process of law.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
7. Interim order granted on 16.12.2020 stands vacated.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
MRS.JUSTICE SUREPALLI NANDA Date:12.07.2023
